content: The USMLE Step 2 Clinical Skills (Step 2 CS) is a component of the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) that is required for all medical students or graduates who wish to obtain a medical license in the United States. This examination evaluates the clinical skills of candidates through a series of simulated patient encounters. The Step 2 CS exam consists of 12 patient encounters, each lasting 15 minutes, followed by 10 minutes to document a patient note. During these encounters, examinees are required to interact with standardized patients (SPs) to take a detailed history, perform a focused physical examination, and formulate a list of differential diagnoses. The cases presented typically reflect common outpatient or emergency room scenarios across various medical disciplines, including internal medicine, surgery, psychiatry, pediatrics, and obstetrics and gynecology. Examinees are expected to thoroughly investigate the patient’s chief complaint and gather relevant information, including the history of present illness, past medical history, medication use, allergies, social history (such as alcohol, tobacco, drug use, and sexual practices), and family history. The patient note, which differs slightly from a standard SOAP note, requires the documentation of pertinent findings from the history and physical examination. Additionally, examinees must list up to five differential diagnoses and propose up to five diagnostic tests or procedures to further evaluate the patient’s condition. However, treatment recommendations, such as prescribing medications or administering IV fluids, are not included in the patient note. The exam spans an 8-hour day and replaced the ECFMG Clinical Skills Assessment (CSA) on June 14, 2004. The last administration of the CSA occurred on April 16, 2004. The Step 2 CS is graded on a pass/fail basis, with no numerical score assigned. To pass, candidates must achieve a passing grade in three sub-components: 1. Integrated Clinical Encounter (ICE): This component assesses the examinee’s ability to collect relevant clinical information during the patient encounter and to document an appropriate patient note, including differential diagnoses. The standardized patient evaluates the clinical interaction, while a practicing physician grades the patient note. 2. Communication and Interpersonal Skills (CIS): This component evaluates the examinee’s ability to ask open-ended questions, avoid medical jargon, and refrain from unnecessary repetition. It also assesses the ability to share information effectively, address patient concerns, provide counseling, and demonstrate professionalism. This includes showing empathy, respecting the patient, maintaining proper hygiene during the examination, and ensuring patient comfort. 3. Spoken English Proficiency (SEP): The Step 2 CS exam is administered exclusively in the United States at five Clinical Skills Evaluation Centers (CSEC), located in the following cities: Atlanta, Georgia Chicago, Illinois Houston, Texas Los Angeles, California Philadelphia, Pennsylvania
